# Jubilees Chapter 50 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The absolute Sabbath — the most stringent day of rest in any ancient Jewish text; the book closes

---

**50:1** "After these laws, I revealed to you the Sabbaths of the land — the Sabbath years and the jubilees — going all the way back to Adam. The LORD commanded you: keep the Sabbath as a day of rest.

**50:2** Anyone who does any of the following on the Sabbath will die: any work; any journey; any commercial activity; drawing water that wasn't prepared the day before; picking up any load and carrying it out of your tent or your house.

**50:3** Nothing shall be done on the Sabbath except what was prepared on the sixth day — eating and drinking, resting, observing the Sabbath from all work, blessing the LORD your God who gave you this festival day, this holy day, this day of the sacred kingdom for all Israel.

**50:4** The Sabbath is greater than every other day. On it you are to be holy. Rest completely.

**50:5** Anyone who violates the Sabbath — anyone who does any work on it — will die. Anyone who treats it as ordinary will die.

**50:6** No fire in any dwelling on the Sabbath. No cooking on the Sabbath. All food preparation must be done on the sixth day, before the Sabbath begins.

**50:7** Nothing carried in or out of the house on the Sabbath.

**50:8** Nothing moved from one house to another on the Sabbath.

**50:9** Nothing done on the Sabbath except blessing the LORD your God.

**50:10** Anyone who picks up a load and carries it out of his dwelling on the Sabbath — death.

**50:11** Anyone who travels on the Sabbath for business or for any purpose other than returning home — death.

**50:12** Anyone who draws a sword, nocks an arrow, or picks up any weapon of war on the Sabbath — death.

**50:13** Anyone who traps or catches an animal, a bird, or a fish on the Sabbath — death.

**50:14** Anyone who does any of the following on the Sabbath — death: any kind of work, any travel, plowing a field, tilling the soil, cutting anything, lighting a fire, loading a pack animal, sailing a boat, striking or killing anything, slaughtering a beast or bird, catching a fish. And — remarkably — fasting. And waging war.

**50:15** All these are forbidden. The Sabbath legislation must be observed exactly as written in the tablets given to me to record for you — the law for every appointed time.

**50:16** And this is the end of the account of all the divisions of the days. From creation to the new creation — when heaven and earth and every creature will be remade, when the sky will be transformed and all living things renewed — right up to the day when the LORD's sanctuary will stand in Jerusalem on Mount Zion: every year and every day from that beginning until now is sacred and holy.

**50:17** The complete account of all the divisions of the days, of the law and the testimony, is now finished. You — Moses — received it on Mount Sinai. It will stand until the new creation comes, until the sanctuary of the LORD is built in Jerusalem forever."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 50 is the most remarkable chapter in Jubilees. The Sabbath legislation goes further than any other ancient Jewish text: the death penalty is demanded for fasting on the Sabbath (v.14) — because Jubilees understands the Sabbath as a day of joy and plenty, not discipline. This may be directed against early fasting movements. The book closes with a cosmic vision (vv.16-17): all of history, from Adam to the new creation, is organized around the sacred calendar that this book records. The final image — the eternal Jerusalem sanctuary — is the telos of the entire Jubilees project.*
